---
name: project-savannah-simulation
description: Build/test setup for the Australian Savannah predator-prey Java simulation (module_java)
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: d41a047f-20ef-41b9-82b4-a42d098ae7f4

The `module_java` worktrees contain a BlueJ-style predator-prey simulation (default package, no build file). Core model: `Actor` → `Consumer`/`Producer` → concrete species; `Field`/`Location` grid; `Simulator` orchestrates; `SimulatorView` (Swing) + `StatisticsView` (JavaFX).

**Build:** JavaFX is NOT installed in this environment, so `javac *.java` fails only on `Simulator.java` + `StatisticsView.java` (javafx imports). The model compiles cleanly. To get a full local compile, write minimal stub classes for the javafx symbols used and compile with `-cp <stubs>` — the rest of the project is plain Java/Swing/AWT.

**Deterministic testing:** `Randomizer` uses a fixed seed (10001) via `Randomizer.reset()`, so `Simulator.populate()` placement is reproducible and can be regression-hashed. Caveat: `Gender.getRandom()` uses `Math.random()` (NOT the seeded RNG), so exclude gender from any golden-value comparison.

**Known latent bugs (left unfixed — would change simulation output):** `Consumer.maxSustenanceLevel` shadows `Actor.maxSustenanceLevel` and stays 0; `Consumer.eat()` uses `consumptionWorth` instead of `actorConsumptionWorth` for leftover food; `Disease.STEPS_BEFORE_DEATH` is `static` (shared across all diseases).

**Variants differ — the `module_java` worktrees are NOT all the same code.** The `R004_module_java` worktree uses a different hierarchy: `Actor` (interface) + abstract `Organism` → `Animal`/`Plant` → concrete species (Deer/Coyote/Wolf/Eagle/Mouse/Grass/Hunter), Swing-only `SimulatorView`, no JavaFX at all (`javac *.java` compiles cleanly with no stubs). Here `Randomizer.getRandomSex()` uses the SEEDED `rand.nextBoolean()` (seed=1), so gender IS deterministic and the whole sim is reproducible — different from the Math.random() caveat above. Latent bugs in this variant: `Disease` propagation/lethality are `static` (last-created disease's values shared by all); `Hunter.alive` is `static` (shared across hunters). Verify behaviour-preserving refactors with a headless harness that mirrors `Simulator.populate()`/`simulateOneStep()` driving the real model classes and FNV-hashes per-step class counts (the view blocks running `Simulator` directly — it constructs a `JFrame`, which HANGS in this no-display env, not just throws). In R004 the model now lives in a view-free `SimulationEngine` (extracted from `Simulator`), so harnesses can drive `new SimulationEngine(160,240); engine.reset(); engine.step()` directly instead of copying the loop.

**Weather determinism — FIXED (was a cross-JVM non-determinism bug).** Historically `Weather.changeWeather()` did `new HashSet<>(Arrays.asList(WeatherType...)).toArray()[randomInt]`; HashSet-of-enum iteration order depends on identity hashCodes, which differ between JVM processes, so the same seed produced different weather sequences (and thus different whole-sim output) in different processes — fingerprints were only comparable WITHIN one process. This was fixed (with the user's explicit OK to change output) by selecting from `WeatherType.values()` (fixed declaration order [RAINING,SUNNY,CLOUDY]); `weatherList`/`addWeatherList` removed. RNG consumption is unchanged (still one `rand.nextInt(3)` per change) and the distribution stays uniform, so only the deterministic trace is pinned — now stable across JVMs. In this env the unperturbed run already iterated in declaration order, so the canonical fingerprint (engine harness, 160x240, 150 steps, position-sensitive sig) is **-2184605646102145951** and is now identical across processes. Verified by perturbing the identity-hashCode PRNG (`System.identityHashCode(new Object())` ×N before building the engine): pre-fix N=0/7/100/5000 gave 4 different fingerprints; post-fix all give -2184605646102145951. Consequence for future work: cross-process fingerprint comparison is now VALID. Still use a POSITION-sensitive signature (class+diseased per cell), not counts-only. Remaining latent bugs (behaviour-changing if fixed): `Disease` propagation/lethality are `static` (shared across all diseases).

content.text:
Done. Each `Disease` now holds its own properties; fix verified and shipped (only `Disease.java` changed, compiles clean).

## The fix

`PROPAGATION_RATE` and `LETHALITY_RATE` were `static`, so every `Disease` returned whatever the **last-constructed** instance happened to set — all concurrent diseases behaved as one. I made them per-instance fields (`propagationRate`, `lethalityRate`), renamed `PROPAGATION_MODE` → `propagationMode` for consistency now that all three are instance state, and made the RNG a local in the default constructor (the per-instance `Random` reference wasn't needed). The public API (`getPropagationRate`/`getLethalityRate`/`getDiseaseType`) is unchanged.

## Impact analysis

**Concrete demonstration:** right after `populate`, **17 diseased organisms exist**. Post-fix they carry **17 distinct (propagation/lethality) pairs** spanning propagation 0.0017–0.5016 and lethality 0.0029–0.3828. Pre-fix, all 17 returned the single last-created pair (~0.50/0.21).

**Effect on the deterministic trace:**
- **Disease creation is unchanged.** The constructor still draws exactly three randoms (propagation, lethality, mode) in the same order, so `populate` produces *byte-identical* diseases in both versions — the same organisms are infected with the same true rates. The fix only changes what the getters *return*, not what the RNG produces at construction.
- **Divergence begins at step 1.** The first disease-rate-dependent check — the engine's per-actor propagation-death test — now evaluates each of the 17 diseased organisms against *its own* rate instead of all against the last-created ~0.50. Death and infection outcomes flip immediately, which changes the field, which cascades. Confirmed empirically: the per-step traces differ from step 1 onward.
- **New fingerprint:** `-8012133067710255676` (was `-2184605646102145951`). It's deterministic and — thanks to last turn's `Weather` fix — stable across JVM processes (verified by repeated fresh runs).

**Statistical / semantic effect:** Before, the model was degenerate — propagation and lethality were effectively one global value, constantly overwritten, so disease severity was arbitrary (whichever disease was constructed most recently). After, diseases are independent with rates distributed propagation ~U[0, 0.6) and lethality ~U[0, 0.4). Disease spread and mortality now reflect each strain's actual properties — the intended, non-degenerate behavior. Aggregate disease prevalence and mortality will differ from before (generally less extreme, since outcomes no longer swing with a single shared rate), but the change is a correctness improvement, not a tuning choice.

I've updated project memory to record the fix and the new canonical fingerprint. With both the `Weather` and `Disease` latent bugs now resolved, I'm not aware of any remaining correctness bugs in the simulation model.
